sources.title: Raypak — Top 7 Start-Up Points for Heaters
quotes: Rodent Inspection: remove them from the heater before attempting to ignite it, as they are highly flammable
Debris Removal: leaves and other organic debris can accumulate inside the heater, which could restrict airflow or inhibit burner combustion
Spider Check: spider webs around the heater periphery might not obstruct combustion, they could indicate the presence of spiders and nests in critical areas like gas jets or burners
Gas Line Examination: Inspect all valves that allow the flow gas and ensure they are open, including gas line shut offs and the heater gas valve switch
Electrical Integrity: Check all electrical connections, ensuring they are secure and free of exposed wires
Seal Openings: ensure any openings used for draining the heater last Fall are securely closed

mechanism.claim: A heater that will not fire is frequently reporting a flow problem, not a heater fault — and the filter is usually what caused it.
mechanism.detail: The heater will not light without proving adequate water flow through its water pressure switch. Hayward's own commissioning instruction is to 'set flow rates above minimum (accounting for a dirty filter)' — meaning the design assumption is that flow FALLS as the filter loads. So a system set up with only marginal headroom passes on a clean filter and drops below the heater's minimum as the filter approaches its backwash point.
mechanism.whyItMatters: It explains the intermittent pattern owners describe and misread: the heater works after a backwash, gets unreliable over the following weeks, then fires perfectly again right after the next clean. That reads as a flaky heater. It is a flow margin problem, and the fix is upstream — clean the filter, check the gauge against the clean baseline.
mechanism.crossRef: Ties EQP-006 (clean starting pressure) and EQP-004 (gauge locates restriction) to a symptom nobody connects to them.

secondDetail_wellSourced: Raypak's start-up list names spider and rodent nests in gas jets and burners as a real cause, and notes rodent nests are 'highly flammable'. Rarely mentioned in consumer content and genuinely explains seasonal first-start failures.

safety_REQUIRED.why: §10 mandates a safety block for gas.
safety_REQUIRED.position: Write the diagnostic boundary hard: an owner may check flow, filter, valve positions, thermostat, power and gas shutoff position. An owner should NOT disassemble the gas train, adjust gas pressure, clean burners on a live appliance, or bypass a safety switch. Combustion work is licensed work in most jurisdictions.
safety_REQUIRED.mustInclude: Smell gas → do not operate switches, leave the area, call the gas utility. Never bypass a pressure or limit switch to make a heater run — those switches are what stop it firing when firing is unsafe.
